'''Rachel Angela Ward''' is an American applied mathematician at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. She is known for work on [[machine learning]], [[optimization]], and [[signal processing]]. 
At the University of Texas, she is W. A. "Tex" Moncrief Distinguished Professor in Computational Engineering and Sciences—Data Science, and professor of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cns.utexas.edu/directory/item/386-ward-rachel-a?Itemid=349|title=Rachel A Ward|work=Directory|publisher=University of Texas College of Natural Sciences|access-date=2021-06-13}}</ref>

==Education==
Ward received her BS in mathematics from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rachel A. Ward|url=https://www.ma.utexas.edu/users/rachel/vitae.pdf|accessdate=April 8, 2017}}</ref>  She earned her PhD in applied and [[computational mathematics]] from [[Princeton University]] in 2009. Her doctoral advisor was [[Ingrid Daubechies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rachel Angela Ward|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=144607|publisher=Mathematics Genealogy Project|accessdate=April 8, 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ward was an instructor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]] from 2009-2011<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pacm.princeton.edu/events/pacm-colloquium-rachel-ward-university-texas|title=PACM Colloquium: Rachel Ward, University of Texas|last=|first=|date=19 February 2019|website=Program in Applied & Computational Mathematics, Princeton University|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=8 October 2019}}</ref> and then joined the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin in 2011.<ref name=":0" /> In 2018, she was a Visiting Research Scientist at [[Facebook Artificial Intelligence Research]]<ref name=":0" /> and in 2019 she was a Von Neumann Fellow at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/rachel-ward|title=IAS - Current Van Neumann Fellow: Rachel Ward|last=|first=|date=|website=Institute for Advanced Study|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=8 October 2019}}</ref> She serves on the Scientific Advisory Board for the [[Institute for Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics]] (ICERM).<ref>{{Cite web|title=ICERM - Trustee and Advisory Boards - Trustee & Advisory Boards|url=https://icerm.brown.edu/about/boards/|access-date=2021-07-11|website=icerm.brown.edu}}</ref>

== Research ==
Ward is known for her work across a wide variety of applied math areas including image processing, compressed sensing, and stochastic and adaptive gradient descent.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-11-02 |title=Mathematician Rachel Ward Sees the Big Picture |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2023/11/02/mathematician-rachel-ward-sees-the-big-picture/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> Ward also worked on a project funded by the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]], with faculty from UT Austin's College of Natural Sciences and Cockrell School, to develop [[unmanned aerial vehicle]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.utexas.edu/2018/04/26/new-engineering-project-aims-to-create-ai-for-uavs/|title=Creating Truly Autonomous Systems is the Goal of New $7.5 Million Engineering Project|last=|first=|date=26 April 2018|website=UT News|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=8 October 2019}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Ward was awarded an [[Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship]] in Mathematics in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database}}</ref>
Ward and [[Deanna Needell]] received the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications|IMA]] Prize in Mathematics and Applications in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Deanna Needell and Rachel Ward Co-awarded the 2016 IMA Prize in Mathematics and its Applications|url=https://www.ima.umn.edu/press-room/ima-prize-winners-2016|publisher=IMA|accessdate=April 8, 2017}}</ref> In 2020, Ward was named as a Simons Fellow.<ref name=":1" />  Ward was an invited speaker at the 2022 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Virtual ICM 2022 Sectional Schedule By Day|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/ICM2022/Program/Virtual_ICM_2022_Sectional_Schedule.pdf}}</ref>
